name: Jediael
overview: Jediael was a male Levite known as the second-born son of Meshelemiah, also called Shallum. His role is noted within the tribe of Levi, which was set apart for priestly and temple duties. Beyond his lineage, no additional details or notes are recorded about his life or ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Jediael means 'known of God [El],' reflecting a recognition or relationship with the divine. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a significant theophoric element, highlighting God's acknowledgement or presence.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Jediael was the son of Shallum (Meshelemiah). No other family relationships are documented beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Jediael's biblical significance lies primarily in his identification as a Levite and as the second-born son of Meshelemiah, situating him within the Levitical genealogies important for temple service and worship roles. His mention preserves the lineage and order of Levite families responsible for ministering in the house of God. Although the text does not elaborate on his personal deeds, his inclusion affirms the continuity of God's appointed servants within Israel.
